What the second/third argument of these presentation helpers really carries is the studio render environment (editable / previewState / states Map / entityMetadata), so they became renderEnvironment / coverRenderEnvironment / coverActiveRenderEnvironment / activeRenderEnvironment / awaitingRenderEnvironment / authoredRenderEnvironment / effectLightRenderEnvironment / toggleRenderEnvironment / climateRenderEnvironment / climatePowerRenderEnvironment / airflowRenderEnvironment / labelRenderEnvironment / airflowLayerRenderEnvironment / formattingEnvironment, and the two arguments that are really entity state or path geometry became vacuumMapState / bedPathOutline / historySource.

tools/check_name_kinds.mjs then rejected 2 shapes: ue@19 -> componentRegistry is a new Map() so the name must say Map or By<Key> (it became rendererByComponentType, which is also more accurate: type -> {render}) and value22@97 -> unknownComponentTypeText holds a createElement("span") node (it became unknownComponentTypeElement).

Reusing the previous batch's map builder (/tmp/hb-build-geo1.mjs, copied to /tmp/hb-build-reg1.mjs) looked wrong: String.prototype.replace swaps only the FIRST occurrence of a plain-string needle, so the builder still printed 'WROTE tools/rename-maps/geometry-c1.json' while it was in fact writing registry-c1.json. Verified afterwards that tools/rename-maps/geometry-c1.json was untouched (sha256 still 21d18a45651ef8c0c6dfcf9e1cc0dbfa03855491bc1818d7ee4ace1fc517ae9f, mtime unchanged) and that registry-c1.json holds the registry.js key. Lesson: after adapting a builder, always re-check the shas of both the new map and the map the previous batch already spent.
